_meta.schema: {known_bad: [{id, parent, child, note, expect_pairing}], known_good: [{id, parent, child, note, tolerated, known_defect}]}

contract.tolerated: The pair may MATCH a Sigma rule but must not escalate the verdict above Unknown. Annotating a common pair is acceptable noise.
contract.known_defect: The pair escalates today and should not. A measured, documented failure that is locked in place so it cannot spread — not an excuse. Removing an entry from this list is the fix; adding one requires justifying why it cannot be fixed.

_meta.purpose: Calibration corpus for core.process_analyzer Layer 4 — the sibling of tests/fixtures/cmdline_corpus.json. Closes the 'Option A's false-positive rate is unmeasured' item in docs/process_analyzer_plan.md §7.
sources: known_bad: parent/child combinations named in the process_analyzer plan's own §6 sanity check, plus common webshell and script-engine chains.
known_good: ordinary Windows desktop, service, developer and CI process trees.
notes: `tolerated` marks a benign pair that legitimately matches a Sigma pairing. It records that the finding is annotation-only — a tolerated pair must NOT escalate the module's verdict above Unknown. That is the distinction this corpus enforces: annotating a common pair is acceptable noise, calling it Suspicious is not.
1155 of the 1874 shipped pairs come from rules that also required a CommandLine condition. This corpus measures what that costs.

known_bad.note: Macro spawning a shell — the canonical maldoc chain.
WMI provider spawning a shell — lateral movement or remote exec.
IIS worker spawning a shell — the classic webshell signature.
SQL Server spawning a shell — xp_cmdshell abuse.
PDF reader spawning a shell. Currently missed — recorded as a known gap rather than removed.

known_good.note: User opens a command prompt from the shell. Matches a LNK-pattern rule whose real signal was the dropped CommandLine condition; annotation only.
Administrator opens PowerShell. Same shape as above.
Clicking a link in an email — benign, unlike outlook -> cmd.

A Gradle or Maven build step, escalated to Suspicious by 'Webshell Detection With Command Line Keywords'. java.exe sits in the webserver rule family alongside w3wp/nginx/php-cgi because Java web servers exist — but java.exe is also every desktop Java app and every CI build. The rule relied on a CommandLine keyword to tell a webshell from a build step, and that is exactly what Option A dropped. Not fixed: suppressing commandline-constrained rules would also silence w3wp/nginx/php-cgi, whose escalating pairings are 100% commandline-constrained and are true positives.
Windowless JVM, same rule and same reasoning as java.exe.
CI agent running a build step.
Scheduled task running a vendor binary.
SQL Server's own agent — unlike sqlservr -> cmd.
IIS worker launching a .NET host — not a shell.
Office re-entry, not a shell spawn.
